Indian Standard 

FLOW MEASUREMENT OF NATURAL GAS 
BY ROTARY PISTON METERS 



ICS 75.160.30; 75.180.30 



© BIS 2006 

BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS 

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 
NEW DELHI 110002 



June 2006 Price Group 3 



Weights and Measures Sectional Committee, PG 26 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Weights and 
Measures Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production and General Engineering Division Council. 

This standard is formulated for measuring the gas consumption at the user's end, when the gas is supplied through 
the pipelines. In order to meet the requirement by the users only the Bureau of Indian Standards, has formulated 
the above Indian Standard for accuracy of metering system to fulfill the consumer satisfaction. This standard 
used for custody transfer of natural gas. 

In preparing this standard considerable assistance has been derived from the following publication: 

IS 1 4439 (Part 3) : 1 998 Legal metrology — Gas volume meters: Part 3 Rotary piston and turbine gas meters 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1 9*60 
'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'.

Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India 



IS 15673 : 2006 



Indian Standard 

FLOW MEASUREMENT OF NATURAL GAS 
BY ROTARY PISTON METERS 



1 SCOPE 

This standard specifies the requirements for the 
construction, methods of pressure tapping, working 
ranges widi nominal values of minimum/maximum flow 
rates and permissible errors for rotary piston meters. 

2 REFERENCE 

The standard listed below contains provision which 
through reference in this text, constitutes provision 
of this standard. At the tune of publication, the edition 
indicated was valid. All standards are subject to 
revision and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent edition of the standard 
indicated below: 

IS No. Title 

14439 (Part 1) : Legal metrology — Gas volume 
1997 meters: Part 1 General requirements 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

For the purpose of this standard, the following 
terminology shall apply. 

3.1 Rotary Piston Meters, are those, in which internal 
walls defining the measuring chambers are set in rotation 
and the number of revolutions of these walls represents 
a measurement of the volume of the gas passed. 



4 WORKING RANGE 

The nominal values of the maximum flowrates and the 
corresponding minimum flowrates of rotary piston 
meters are given in Table 1 . 

5 MATERIAL FOR CONSTRUCTION 

5.1 Material 

The material for construction of the gas meters and 
its components shall be as specified in IS 14439 
(Part 1). 

5.2 Details of Construction 

5.2. 1 Rotary piston meters shall have a static pressure 
tapping at the inlet and at the outlet, close to the 
connection (flange) for measuring the pressure 
absorption, the pressure measured upstream shall 
constitute the metering pressure. Length between the 
ends of its inlet and outlet connection shall be less than 
or equal to S times nominal connection. 

5.2.2 Rotary piston gas meters may include a manual 
device for allowing the pistons to be turned, provided 
that it cannot be improperly used in such a way to 
interfere with the correct functioning of the gas meter. 

5.2.3 Notwithstanding the requirements given in 9 of 
IS 14439 (Part 1) the bearings of the shafts of the

rotating pistons of gas meters (roots type) of a size

as to allow them to be replaced without damaging the

5.3 Pressure Tappings 

5.3.1 The bores for pressure tappings shall have a 
diameter of at least 3 nun. In the case of slit-shaped 
pressure tappings, slits shall have a width of at 
least 2 nun in the dkection of the flows and a cross- 
section of at least 10 mm^. 

5.3.2 Pressure tappings shall be provided with a means 
of closure so as to make them gas-tight. 

5.3.3 The pressure tapping for the metering pressure 
shall be clearly and indelibly marked 'p^ and other 
pressure tappings as 'p\ 

5.4 Built-in Conversion Device 

5.4.1 Rotary piston gas meters may have a built-in 
conversion device which converts the volume at 
metering temperature to that at base temperature or 
which converts the volume at metering conditions to 
that at base conditions. 

5.4.2 The indicating device for the volume at base 
conditions shall have a sufficient number of digits to 
ensure that the volume passed during 2 000 h at 
maximum flowrate, minimum temperature and, if 
applicable, maximum pressure does not move or switch 
all the digits to their initial positions. 

6 TEST ELEMENTS 

6. 1 When the gas meter has a mechanical test element 
according to 6.2.2 of IS 14439 (Part 1), the scale 
interval and the scale numbering shall be according to 
Table 2. 

6.2 The scale interval of the test element of the 
indicating device for base conditions shall be less 
than 0.1 percent of the converted volume counted 
in 3 min with the maximum flowrate at maximum 
temperature and, if applicable, minimum pressure.

7.1 Under the conditions laid down in 7 of IS 14439 
(Part 1), the maximum permissible errors applicable 
to all the gas meters shall be as follows:

8 PATTERN APPROVAL 

8.1 Request for Pattern Approval 

8. 1 . 1 Manufacturer shall submit the sample for pattern 
approval to the appropriate authority. Manufacturer 
shall place two to six samples manufactured in 
conformity with the pattern at the disposal of the 
authority responsible for examination. 

8.1.2 If so requested by the authority responsible for the 
examination, these meters should include more than one 
size, if simultaneous approval of those sizes is requested. 

8.1.3 Depending on the results of the tests, additional 
sample meters may be requested. 

8.1.4 Notwithstanding the above requirements, the 
sample meters may be submitted at different times, but 
the decision regarding pattern approval will be given only 
when all these sample meters have been received and 
examined. 

8.2 Tests 

8.2.1 General 

The pattern and its sample meters shall comply with 
the requirement of IS 14439 (Part 1) and 4, 5, 6 and 7 
of this standard. 

In addition, for flowrates, between 0.4 q^^^ and q^^^ 
the difference between the maximum and minimum 
of the error curve as a function of the flowrate 'q' shall 
not exceed 1 percent for each meter. 

8.2.2 Disturbance Test for Rotary Piston Meters 

Rotary piston meters shall be subjected to a test for the 
influence of flow disturbances as specified in Annex A. 
During the test the shift of the error curve shall not 
exceed 0.33 percent. 



If the design of a rotary piston meter pattern is similar 
for all the pipe sizes, disturbance tests with gas meters 
of two sizes shall suffice. 

8.2.3 Durability Test 

The pattern and samples of rotary piston gas meters 
shall be subjected to a durability test. This test shall be 
carried out as far as possible at the maximum flowrate 
and with air or gas. The duration of the durability test 
shall be such that each gas meter measures a volume of 
air or gas corresponding to 1 000 h of operation of the 
gas meter at the maximum flowrate. The test shall be 
completed within two months. 

After the durability test, the gas meters, when tested 
with air of density 1.2 kg/m^ using the same standard 
instruments as those used in the test resulting from 8.2. 1 
shall comply with the following requirements: 

a) The values of the errors determined at the flow- 
rates specified in 9.2.1 shall not differ by more 
than 0.5 percent from the errors noted during 
the test resulting from 8.2.1. 

b) For flowrates between *0.4 q^^^' and 'q^Jy 
the difference between the maximum and 
minimum of the error curve as a function of 
the flowrate 'q' shall not exceed 1.5 percent. 

8.2.4 Gas Meters with Drive Shafts 

In the case of rotary piston gas meters having one or 
more drive shafts, at least three meters of each size 
shall be tested with air at a density of 1 .2 kg/m^ for 
compliance with the requirements of 4.3.2.4 of 
IS 14439 (Part 1) and 7.4 of this standard. 

In case of rotary piston gas meters having several drive 
shafts, the test shall be carried out on the drive shaft 
which gives the least favourable result. 

Where a pattern embraces gas meters of various sizes, 
the torque test need be carried out only on the meters 
of the smallest size, provided that the same torque is 
specified for the larger gas meters and that the output 
shafts of the latter have the same or greater output 
constants. 

In the case of gas meters with several values for ^Min' 
only the test described in 8.2.1 for the least value of 
'^Min* "^^^ ^ carried out. The permissible torques for 
the other working ranges may be calculated from that 
test result. 

Conversion to other 'q^,^' values is governed by the 
following rules: 

a) Where the flow is constant, the variation in 
the error is proportional to the torque, and 

b) Where the torque is constant, the variation in 



IS 15673 : 2006 



the error for rotary piston gas meters is 
inversely proportional to the flowrate, and for 
turbine gas meters it is inversely proportional 
to the square of the flowrate. 

9 INITIAL VERIFICATION AND SUBSEQUENT 
VERIFICATIONS 

9.1 Examination 

9.1.1 Gas meters shall be examined and tested to 
ascertain whether they conform in general to their 
approved patterns. They shall comply with the 
requirements of IS 14439 (Part 1) as well as the 
requirements of this standard. 

9.1.2 Gas meters shall be submitted in working 
order and shall be provided with the required sites 
for the application of the verification and protective 
marks. 

9. 1 .3 If gas meters are intended to incorporate ancillary 
devices operated by the output shafts, these devices 
shall be attached, unless attachment after verification 
is expressly authorized. 

9.2 Accuracy Tests and Calibration 

9.2.1 A gas meter shall be considered to comply with 
the requirements concerning the maximum permissible 
errors, if these are met at the following flowrates: 

a) For gas meters with a working range of 1 : 10 
to 1 : 30 : q^,. 0.05 q^^ and 0.1 ty^^when 
these values are larger than q^^^, 0.25 q^^^, 
0.40 ^^^,0.70 (7^^ and (7^^, and 

b) For gas meters with a working range of 
1-50: ^^,,0.05(^^^,0.15 (7^^,0.25 .7^^, 
0.40 (7^^,0.70^^^ and ^^^. 

If the tests are done at other flowrates, they shall be at 
least as effective as those mentioned above. 

9.2.2 A gas meter may be verified using a gas other 
than air, and/or at other than near ambient conditions. 

9.3 Additional Markings 

The density range in which the errors are required to 



comply with the maximum permissible errors may be 
indicated on the data plate, expressed as: 

p = .... to .... kg/m^ 

This marking shall replace the range of metering 
pressures [5.1(i) of IS 14439 (Part 1)], unless the 
pressure marking refers to a built-in conversion device. 

10 MARKING 

10.1 Each gas meter shall bear the markings 
conforming to IS 14439 (Part 1). 

10.2 BIS Certification Marking 

The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 

10.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 
The details of conditions under which the licence for 
the use of Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 

11 PACKING 

The gas meter shall be wrapped in dust proof paper 
and placed in the wooden/corrugated box with 
sufficient packing material all around to prevent any 
risk of damage or deformation during transit. 

a) Before preparation for packing, each meter 
shall be dried and cleaned. 

b) Meter openings shall be covered to prevent 
the entry of dirt and other foreign matter, 
threaded and machined surfaces shall be well 
covered with rust preventive coatings. 

c) Flanges and exposed thread connections shall 
be well protected over their entire surface by 
providing the suitable protectors. 

1 2 INSTRUCTIONS FOR INSTALLATION AND 
MAINTENANCE 

Installation and maintenance instructions, including 
for routine checks, shall be provided by the 
manufacturer.

ANNEX A 

(Clause 8.2.2) 

DISTURBANCE TEST FOR ROTARY PISTON METERS 



A-1 GENERAL 



A-1.1 The test specified in this annex shall be carried 
out with air at clause to ambient conditions at flowrates 
of0.25^^„^,0.4(7^.^,and^^.^. 

A- 1. 2 If the design of the pattern of the gas meter is 
similar for all pipe sizes, it is sufficient to perform the 
test on two sizes. Similarity of sizes is assumed if the 
values of HID and SIL (see Fig. 1 ) for any size of meter 
are equal to or less than those for the tested meters. 

A.2 MILD DISTURBANCES 

A-2.1 The piping configurations [see Fig. 2(a) 
and 2(b)] consist of a pipe with a nominal diameter 
DN^ and with a length of 5 DN^, two elbows with radius 
DN^ not in the same plane and a concentric expander 
with diameter DN^ and DN and a length between DN 
and 1.5 DM 

The values of DN, in relation to the values of DN arc

A-2.2 The test shall be carried out with the piping 
configurations as described in A-2.1 installed 2 DN 
upstream of the meter inlet [see Fig. 2(c)] or with a 
4onger upstream straight pipe and/or flow conditioner, 
if so specified by the manufacturer. 

In the latter case the necessary upstream straight pipe 
and/or flow conditioner shall be considered part of the 
approved pattern and specified in the approval certificate. 

A-2.3 During the test the shift of the error curve of the 
meter shall not exceed 0.33 percent. 

A-3 SEVERE DISTURBANCES 

A-3.1 The same piping configuration as specified 
in A-2.1 is used with the addition of a half pipe area 
plate as shown in Fig. 3 installed between the two 
elbows with the opening toward the outside radius of 
the first bend. 

A-3.2 The provisions of A-2.2 and A-2.3 shall apply 
accordingly.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
*BIS Catalogue' and 'Standards : Monthly Additions'.
